syntax.syntax_item: [U, V, X, C, S] = gsvd(A, B)
[U, V, X, C, S] = gsvd(A, B, 'econ')

param_input_item.param_description: an m-by-p single or double matrix.
an n-by-p single or double matrix.
economy-size U, V, C and S.

param_output_item.param_description: generalized singular values sqrt(diag(C'*C) ./ diag(S'*S)) in increasing order.
a p-by-q matrix, q being the rank of [A; B].
nonnegative diagonal matrices with C'*C + S'*S = eye(q).

description.p: [U, V, X, C, S] = gsvd(A, B) returns A = U*C*X' and B = V*S*X'. The diagonal of C increases and the diagonal of S decreases.
When m < q, the nonzero values of C are on the diagonal that starts at column q - m + 1; the values of S are always on its main diagonal.
sigma = gsvd(A, B) returns the generalized singular values; a zero value of S gives Inf.
The decomposition comes from a column-pivoted QR factorization of [A; B], which sets q, followed by a cosine-sine decomposition of its orthogonal factor.
